A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CellCLIP and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering. v3 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original cross-modal retrieval, CP-JUMP1 matching, RxRx3-core relationship-recovery experiments, and component ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds prompt, attention-removal, text-encoder size, and domain-pretraining studies.

M1.justification: Equation (5) revises the written CWCL objective from p_i·q_i to p_i·q_j inside the similarity-weighted sum. The architecture, pooling procedure, and default BERT encoder remain unchanged. This corrects the reported loss without establishing that its implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The three principal datasets and retrieval tasks remain. v3 adds DrugBank descriptions as auxiliary prompt data for matched Bray compounds, reportedly covering about 10% of compounds (Section 5.1, Table 3). This is a limited addition of input data, rather than a new benchmark domain.

E2.justification: v3 Table S.8 adds evaluated BiomedBERT and KV-PLM alternatives to the original BERT perturbation encoder. The headline comparisons with CLOOME variants, MolPhenix*, OpenPhenom-S/16, and ViT-L/16 retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 revises Bray's reported size from 759,782 images/30,404 compounds to 284,034/10,578, retaining the 70/10/20 split and 2,115-compound test set. CP-JUMP1's raw-channel description changes from nine to eight; processed inputs remain five-channel. New studies introduce prompt-removal, top-n deletion, and smaller-encoder settings. These substantially revise reported settings, but reruns are unestablished, and v3 Appendix D inconsistently gives 28.4k images/10.8k compounds.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's existing backbone, pooling-operator, loss, and retrieval-threshold analyses, v3 tests individual prompt components and DrugBank enrichment, removal of highly attended instances, BERT parameter size, and domain-adapted encoders (Table 3; Tables S.3, S.7–S.8). These substantially expand empirical examination of the framework's design choices.

E5.justification: The new checklist's item 7 claims cross-modal confidence intervals and biological-task means/standard deviations across time points, perturbation types, and cell types. However, retrieval captions still specify standard deviations across seeds, and the biological benchmark table retains point estimates. This adds inconsistent statistical reporting text; no increased run count or defined confidence-interval procedure is established.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and appendix tables retain their numerical values after matching renumbering. Substantial new results concern the added ablations: v3 Table 3 reports perturbation-to-profile R@10 of 1.26% without SMILES versus 7.37% with the original prompt; Table S.3 reports R@1 reaching zero after removing five highest-attention instances. Tables S.7–S.8 add encoder-size and encoder-type results. These are new condition-specific findings, not demonstrated v2-to-v3 performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation (5)'s q_i-to-q_j correction changes mathematical substance: in v2, the normalized similarity weights cancel because the logarithmic term is independent of j; v3 makes that term depend on the weighted pair. The other displayed equations are unchanged, with no added theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: text-based perturbation representation, CrossChannelFormer, stronger retrieval and biological-task performance, and computational efficiency. The new experiments support existing headline claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning SMILES informativeness, limited DrugBank coverage, attention selecting instances with strong perturbation effects, and the roles of encoder capacity and domain pretraining. The existing limitations concerning wet-lab validation and proprietary data remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds experiment-specific hyperparameter grids for retained architecture ablations and CP-JUMP1 evaluations. v3 also specifies text-encoder parameter sizes and discloses CP-JUMP1 subsampling. Conversely, Appendix D removes the earlier exact Bray training, validation, and test image counts. These are documentation changes without established reruns.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for DrugBank, compact pretrained models, KV-PLM's molecule/text work, and BioMedCLIP. These accompany the new prompt and encoder studies; the broader positioning against prior Cell Painting representation and contrastive-learning methods remains intact.

P1.justification: Section 5.1 receives localized explanatory additions, Appendix A gains three subsections, and a NeurIPS checklist is appended. The original narrative and section order are largely retained. The first-page footer changes from a preprint notice to the NeurIPS conference designation.

P2.justification: v3 adds four ablation tables: Table 3 and Tables S.3, S.7, and S.8. Retained tables are resized or repositioned, including Tables S.1–S.2 appearing before the appendix heading, and Figure S.2 is rescaled. Existing figure content and the overall visual style are preserved.

improvement.justification: The new prompt, encoder, and attention-removal experiments provide better evidence for design choices that v2 supported less directly. The loss-index correction and fuller tuning documentation also improve technical clarity. These gains support a limited overall improvement, although v3's conflicting Bray dataset counts and checklist uncertainty claims weaken reproducibility and reporting consistency.
